intents.already_paid: The member says they have already paid.
intents.restructure: The member asks for a payment arrangement or lower payments.
intents.too_much: The member says the full overdue amount is too much.
intents.human: The member asks for a person.

lines.opening: Good day, this is the automated assistant of Northwind Credit Union.
lines.scam: If you have any doubt, please call the number on the back of your card.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I have confirmed I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with the member.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, this will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask_time: Which day and time would suit, on one of the next two business days between 9 am and 5 pm?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, we can only call back on one of the next two business days, between 9 am and 5 pm. Could you suggest another time?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.id_intro: Before we continue, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_explain: We ask these questions to protect your savings, and I cannot continue without them.
lines.id_declined: I'm sorry, I cannot continue without confirming your identity.
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I could not confirm your identity. Please visit any branch with photo ID.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I am calling about overdue payments.
lines.product_line: Your {name} is {days} days overdue, with {amount} overdue.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay everything that is overdue today?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, the lowest amount I can accept is {floor}.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, the date needs to be today or later. Which date could you pay?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}.
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day could you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: To repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {deadline}, so I have used that date.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your payment promise is booked.
lines.sms_line: A confirmation letter will follow by post.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a system fault.
lines.paid_line: Thank you. It can take two business days for a payment to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I will not ask you for a payment on this today.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. Would you like me to connect you with our welfare team?
lines.restructure_line: I will connect you with our arrangements team.
lines.human_ask_help: I can help with most things on this call. What would you like to do?
lines.transfer: I am transferring you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?

lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I could not book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Is that correct, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.

assumptions: The brief names no currency. I used the default 'dollars' because amounts are 'rounded to cents'.
Wrong answers: the API says three end the check, but the brief (§9) says two in total. The brief is the more specific rule, so max_wrong = 2.
Rule 14 says 'Next Monday' means the first Monday after today, so date_rules.next_weekday = 'upcoming'.
Callbacks: 'any of the next two business days (not today)' became within_business_days:2 with business_days_only true. The window is 09:00-17:00 inclusive, and the callback must be after now.
Rule 6 says ask once more after the first bad time, so callback.max_asks = 2. Rule 3.2 says 'ask one more time', so confirm.max_asks = 2.
The brief gives the confirmation question as 'May I speak with {first_name} {last_name}?'. The engine's default title/last_name form is not used.

The verify response fields come from the API: passed = this answer matched, identity_confirmed = all answers passed, remaining_attempts = wrong answers left. The API has no hint field, so hints are empty and response.hint is ''.
Postcode is kind 'upper' with no fixed length, because the brief and API give none. It is sent in capitals without spaces. Birth year is kind 'year' (four digits per the API).
Rule 10 says explain once that the check protects their savings, then a second refusal ends the call. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining (default kept).
The floor is 25% of the overdue amount (floor_pct 25) for every product type. The brief calls it the 'minimum acceptable amount', so floor_names use 'minimum amount'.

The 1-10 day band has one attempt, so it uses only ladder step 1 (full, or the minimum if the member said the full amount is too much, on the deadline). The other bands use step 1 and then step 2 (the minimum on the deadline).

If a computed deadline is not a business day (for example 10 calendar days after today falling on a weekend or closure day), it moves to the previous business day, so promises stay on or before the deadline and on a business day. Rule 13's 'offer the next business day' applies to dates the member proposes before the deadline.
first_ask = 'today', per rule 16 ('First ask whether they can pay everything today'). A plain no is a refusal.
Notes are on: rule 26 requires add_note for every product without a promise, and no notes after a transfer.
Already paid: 'settled' needs no detail per the API, so its reason is ''. With several products, each paid product gets the note already_paid.
Rule 20 says 'If it fails twice' for create_promise, so service_error = declined / system_fault with note system_fault.
Rule 20 prescribes 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' after a booked promise. It is used as sms_line.
The brief does not say whether a recorded promise can be changed. promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.

Defaults kept where the brief is silent: ask_anything_else true, clamp_single_date true, continue after paid or dispute true (rules 21-22 say continue with the others), human.ask_first true (rule 24 says offer help once), max_not_talk 2, date_order 'dmy'.
The brief gives no wording for the dispute line, so the dispute line just says no payment will be asked for. Rule 22 says no promise for disputes.
Product spoken names come from the API product types: credit_card -> 'credit card ending {card_last4}', overdraft, auto_loan.
The scam line follows rule 25 (call the number on the back of your card). It does not mention the debt or the account.
